title: Shree Charani and Shafali Verma Power India Into Asian Games Cricket Semifinal
excerpt: India chased 58 in five overs to beat Japan by eight wickets in Nisshin, setting up a Sunday semifinal with Bangladesh, while the mixed doubles teqball pair reached the bronze-medal match.
body:
• India bowled Japan out for 57 in 19.5 overs, then chased the target in five overs to win the quarter-final by eight wickets at Korogi Athletic Park in Nisshin.
  • Shree Charani took 4 for 10, Shafali Verma hit an unbeaten 40 off 15 balls and Shreyanka Patil marked her comeback with a wicket.
  • The defending champions face Bangladesh in semifinal 2 on Sunday at 10:30 AM IST — a rematch of the Asia Cup semifinal India won by 40 runs on September 10.
  • In teqball, India’s mixed doubles pair Quimcy D’Souza and Mohamed Anas Beg beat the Philippines in the repechage to reach Sunday’s bronze-medal match — India’s first-ever Asian Games medal shot in the sport.

Defending champions India stormed into the semifinals of the Asian Games women’s T20 cricket tournament on Friday, crushing hosts Japan by eight wickets in the quarter-final at Korogi Athletic Park in Nisshin. Needing just 58 to win, Harmanpreet Kaur’s side got home in five overs, with 90 balls to spare, in the first-ever T20 international between the two women’s teams.

“A convincing 8 wicket victory for India in the quarter-final to seal a spot in the final four.”

— WomenCricketHQ, on X

Charani and Shafali run the show

The damage was done up front. Japan were skittled for 57 in 19.5 overs, undone by India’s spinners on a surface offering turn. Shree Charani was the pick of the attack, claiming 4 for 10 from her four overs, including two maidens. Shafali Verma doubled up her batting heroics with 2 for 13, while Shreyanka Patil — back from injury — took 1 for 8, and Deepti Sharma picked up a wicket. Japan’s best resistance came from Ayaka Kato-Stafford, whose 25 off 47 balls was the only innings to reach double figures.

The chase was a formality. Shafali smashed 40 not out off 15 balls, with six fours and two sixes, and sealed the win with a maximum off Shimako Kato. Richa Ghosh finished 12 not out off six. The only blemishes were the early wickets of Gunalan Kamalini, dismissed for a duck, and Bharti Fulmali for six.

A title defence taking shape

India arrived in Nagoya as the defending champions, having won gold at Hangzhou 2023 — beating Bangladesh in the semifinal and Sri Lanka by 19 runs in the final. This campaign matters beyond the medal count: it is the team’s first major tournament response to the humiliation of the T20 World Cup 2026 group-stage exit, and so far the response has been emphatic. India also lifted the Asia Cup earlier this month, and the Nagoya squad carries that momentum.

Sunday’s semifinal opponent is familiar. Bangladesh reached the last four without playing a ball — their quarter-final against China was washed out, and they advanced on a higher ICC ranking. India hold a formidable record against them: 22 wins in 25 T20 internationals, including a nine-match winning streak that covers the Asia Cup semifinal on September 10, when India won by 40 runs.

Teqball pair eye history

Friday also delivered a breakthrough in teqball, which is making its Asian Games debut. India’s mixed doubles pair — Quimcy Joaquim D’Souza and Mohamed Anas Imran Beg — beat the Philippines’ Jhoana Abulencia and Prince Agustin 2-0 (12-3, 12-6) in the repechage at the Nagoya City Higashi Sports Center, earning a place in Sunday’s bronze-medal match. India have never won an Asian Games teqball medal, so a win would be historic.

The pair’s route was winding: third place in Group A, a quarter-final defeat to Vietnam’s Gia Nghi Trinh and Hoang Minh Tan Nguyen (7-12, 10-12), then the repechage lifeline. There was more Indian success in the sport: D’Souza also reached the women’s singles semifinal — beating Japan’s Yuina Sakamoto and Cambodia’s Koemyean DY — and plays Indonesia’s Ima Sumaya on Saturday.

What to watch next

Semifinal 2 between India and Bangladesh is scheduled for Sunday at 10:30 AM IST (2:00 PM local), broadcast live on the Sony Sports Network and streamed on SonyLIV. Pakistan and Sri Lanka contest the other semifinal. The bronze-medal match is on September 22 at 9:00 AM local, with the gold-medal match at 2:00 PM.

For the large Indian community following the Games from Nagoya to New Jersey, the storylines are compelling: a title defence gathering pace, a semifinal grudge match, and a possible first-ever teqball medal for India.
image_caption: Shafali Verma and Shree Charani starred as India crushed Japan in the Asian Games women’s T20 quarter-final at Nisshin. Charani took 4 for 10 and Shafali hit 40 not out off 15 balls as India reached the semifinal with an eight-wicket win.
